subproblem.title: Finiteness of the integer cube chains with bounded coefficients on grid cells inside a compact set (parent step 2)
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, let K ⊆ ℝ^P be compact, let ρ > 0 be real and let B ∈ ℕ. For p = (z, ι) ∈ ℤ^P × (Fin (m+1) → Fin P) let F_p := {x ∈ ℝ^P : ρz_i ≤ x_i ≤ ρ(z_i + 1) for i ∈ range ι and x_i = ρz_i for i ∉ range ι}. For ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U) let I_p(ω) := ∫_{F_p} ω(x)(e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(m)}) dH^{m+1}(x), where e_j = EuclideanSpace.single j 1 is the j-th standard basis vector. Let 𝒬 be the set of X ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) for which there are a finite set s of such pairs and integers b(p) with F_p ⊆ K and |b(p)| ≤ B for every p ∈ s, and X(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} b(p)·I_p(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U). Then 𝒬 is finite. Conventions: ℝ^P = Euclid P and Hᵈ = μHE[d]. For D ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟^d(D) = TestFormOn D d (smooth d-forms on ℝ^P with compact support contained in D) and 𝒟_d(D) = GeometricCurrentOn D d; ∂X = X.boundary (∂X(ω) = X(dω)). For G ⊆ ℝ^P, M_G(X) = X.massOn G is the supremum of ofReal(X(ω)) over ω ∈ 𝒟^d(D) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x; M(X) = X.mass = M_D(X). An IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in D is the contract structure IMRep D d; R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHᵈ(x); R represents X when X(ω) = R.action(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^d(D); μ_R = R.measure = (Hᵈ⌞M).withDensity θ; X is integer multiplicity (IM, IsIntegerMultiplicity X) if some IMRep in D represents it. For V ⊆ D, ι = testFormOnInclusion regards ω ∈ 𝒟^d(V) as an element of 𝒟^d(D) with the same underlying form, and X⌞V = X.restrictDomain (V ⊆ D) ∈ 𝒟_d(V) is given by X⌞V(ω) = X(ιω). X vanishes off a set K if X(ω) = 0 for every test form ω whose tsupport is disjoint from K.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof. Simon Ch. 6, proof of Theorem 7.2 (chapter-06.txt lines 2056–2090) states that there are only finitely many currents P as in (2), with N depending only on M, W, n, k and ρ.
1. K is compact, hence bounded, so there is D ∈ ℝ with ‖y‖ ≤ D for all y ∈ K (Bornology.IsBounded.exists_norm_le). Put N := ⌈D/ρ⌉ ∈ ℕ (Nat.ceil).
2. If p = (z, ι) satisfies F_p ⊆ K, then |z_i| ≤ N for every i. Let y ∈ ℝ^P be the point with coordinates y_i = ρz_i. For i ∈ range ι, ρz_i ≤ y_i ≤ ρz_i + ρ = ρ(z_i + 1) because ρ > 0; for i ∉ range ι, y_i = ρz_i. So y ∈ F_p ⊆ K and ρ|z_i| = |y_i| ≤ ‖y‖ ≤ D (PiLp.norm_apply_le). Hence |z_i| ≤ D/ρ ≤ N (Nat.le_ceil).
3. Let C_f := {z ∈ ℤ^P : |z_i| ≤ N for all i} × (Fin (m+1) → Fin P). This set is finite: it is Fintype.piFinset of the integer intervals [−N, N] times the finite type Fin (m+1) → Fin P. By step 2, every p with F_p ⊆ K lies in C_f.
4. For e : C_f → ℤ define Φ(e) : 𝒟^{m+1}(U) → ℝ by Φ(e)(ω) := Σ_{q∈C_f} e(q)·I_q(ω). The set E_B := {e : C_f → ℤ : −B ≤ e(q) ≤ B for all q} is finite, being a finite product of finite integer intervals (Set.Finite.pi, Set.finite_Icc). Hence its image Φ(E_B) is a finite set of functions.
5. Let X ∈ 𝒬 with data s and b. By step 3, s ⊆ C_f. Define e(q) := b(q) if q ∈ s and e(q) := 0 otherwise. Then e ∈ E_B, because |b(q)| ≤ B for q ∈ s. For every ω, X(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} b(p) I_p(ω) = Σ_{q∈C_f} e(q) I_q(ω) = Φ(e)(ω). Here the sum over s extends to C_f ⊇ s by terms that are 0 (Finset.sum_subset), and the sum over the finset C_f equals the sum over its subtype (Finset.sum_coe_sort). Thus the function ω ↦ X(ω) lies in Φ(E_B).
6. A current is determined by its values (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), so the map X ↦ (ω ↦ X(ω)) is injective on 𝒟_{m+1}(U). By step 5 it maps 𝒬 into the finite set Φ(E_B). Hence 𝒬 is finite (Set.Finite.subset, Set.Finite.of_finite_image). ∎
proof_key_steps: A cell F_p ⊆ K contains its corner ρz, so |z_i| ≤ ⌈D/ρ⌉ where D bounds the norms on K; hence only the finitely many index pairs in C_f are admissible.
Rewrite each admissible chain as a sum over the finite index set C_f, with coefficients in [−B, B] that are zero off s.
Finitely many coefficient vectors give finitely many functionals, and a current is determined by its values, so 𝒬 is finite.

audit.reason: The corner rho*z bounds every admissible integer coordinate, yielding finitely many index pairs. Zero extension of coefficients gives finitely many bounded coefficient vectors; current extensionality then proves finiteness. Unbounded coefficients outside s cause no problem. Omitting StrictMono matches the prose and gives a finite superset sufficient for the parent.
